solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quirky caption about leader of Lords Spiritual?

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled word goes round the single letter
quirky means odd or eccentric, so the letters of the next word are jumbled
the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from Lords

explanation.surface: Someone writes an odd caption beneath a picture of the senior bishop in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords Spiritual' are the bishops in the House of Lords, but the definition is 'Spiritual' alone. 'Quirky' turns CAPTION into PATONIC, and 'about' wraps it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Love that is non-physical and purely of the mind or soul is described by this adjective, after the philosopher Plato.

clue.text: Subject, for example, in piece of fiction

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a lie is an untruth, a piece of fiction
EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A loyal subject is cited as an example within a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal terms a vassal owing allegiance to a lord was called by this word, so it can mean a subject.

clue.text: History of song on disc?

parts.note: a track is one song on an album
a record is a vinyl disc

explanation.surface: A music fan asks for the backstory of a song put on a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's past performance or history of achievements is called by this phrase.

clue.text: It's not easy providing a spread indoors?

definitions.meaning: the idiom says a task is hard work
a picnic is a meal spread outdoors, so one laid out inside is no such thing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a difficult task; literally, a meal served indoors is not an outdoor meal on a rug.

clue.text: Series of adverts showing business opportunity

definitions.meaning: the interval in a TV programme filled with advertisements
read literally, a ... is a lucky chance in trade

explanation.definitionFit: The pause in broadcasting for adverts, and literally a trading opportunity or lucky chance in business.

clue.text: Extremely inexpensive pile acquired by company

indicators.note: acquired by says the company holds the pile inside it

parts.note: a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: A firm buys up a heap of property for very little money.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal adjective for something very cheap and of low quality, an extremely low-cost item.

clue.text: Rodent circling it, a hole

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the rodent surrounds the other word

parts.note: a cavy is a guinea pig, a South American rodent
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal scurries round and round a hole in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow space or pit in a surface or a tooth is a synonym for a hole.

clue.text: Part of cereal plant to get cut

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened by losing its final letter

parts.note: to earn is to get money by working

explanation.surface: A farmer needs a bit of the wheat plant to be harvested.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed-bearing head or spike of a grain crop such as wheat or corn.

clue.text: Striking place around London station? Not very

indicators.note: around means the place abbreviation surrounds the rest

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation of place, as in street names

indicators.note: not very says the letter standing for very, V, is removed

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway terminus

explanation.surface: Someone describes a dramatic scene around a London railway station as not very striking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very' tells you to drop the V, the usual abbreviation for very; 'around' puts the place abbreviation on either side of what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vivid, like a picture, giving a strong visual impression, as in graphic description.

clue.text: Leave suddenly, half of Deal affected

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: camp means affected or exaggerated in manner

explanation.surface: A person quits abruptly, half the agreement having been compromised.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack up and depart in haste or secretly, synonymous with leaving all at once.

clue.text: Unorthodox type, male, to declare decision when heading off

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert

indicators.note: heading off says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a pick is a choice or decision

explanation.surface: An independent-minded man states his ruling and then leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent-minded nonconformist; the word came from an unbranded calf in Texas.

clue.text: Useless person's short jacket, not trendy

indicators.note: not says the trendy word is removed

parts.note: a jerkin is a short close-fitting jacket
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A hopeless fellow wears an unfashionable cropped coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang insult for a foolish or contemptible person, an idiot.

clue.text: City not backing London-born writer

parts.note: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, England

indicators.note: backing says the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A northern English city declines to support an author from London.
explanation.walkthrough: G K Chesterton, creator of Father Brown, was born in Kensington.
explanation.definitionFit: G K Chesterton, author of the Father Brown stories, was born in Kensington, London.

clue.text: Ruthless plutocrat and peer going after thief

indicators.note: going after places the peer behind the thief

parts.note: a robber is a thief
a baron is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A greedy rich man and a nobleman pursue a burglar.
explanation.definitionFit: A term for a nineteenth-century American industrialist who grew rich by unscrupulous methods.

clue.text: I can't remember new names before first clue given

indicators.note: new says the letters of names are made fresh, rearranged

parts.note: the first clue in a grid is one across, I for one and AC for across

explanation.surface: Someone complains that they forget new names before even the first hint is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns NAMES into AMNES; 'first clue' is 1 across, written I AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suffering memory loss might well say this phrase, so it describes such a sufferer.

clue.text: Get artist to enter The Red Planet in carnival

indicators.note: to enter puts the two pieces inside the planet

parts.note: Mars is called the Red Planet
to dig something is slang for getting or understanding it
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a painter to Mars during a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' here is the slang sense, to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday festival celebrated with a carnival, as in New Orleans and Rio.

clue.text: No end of prime French cheese

indicators.note: no end of says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to prime someone is to brief them in advance

explanation.surface: There is plenty of top-quality cheese from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft creamy cheese named after a region east of Paris, an example of French cheese.

clue.text: Act I put on for Greek god

parts.note: to pose is to act or pretend
to don a garment is to put it on

explanation.surface: An actor dresses up to play a god from Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of the sea, counterpart of the Roman Neptune.

clue.text: Group of musicians, patriots at heart

indicators.note: at heart says the middle letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Musicians who are loyal to their country deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: Three performers playing together form a small musical ensemble.

clue.text: What Everest is, most importantly

definitions.meaning: the highest mountain stands higher than every other peak
a phrase meaning first and foremost

explanation.definitionFit: Literally higher than every other summit, and idiomatically meaning first and foremost, chiefly.

clue.text: Stiffness shown by sailor in school

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the school

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A rigid manner displayed by a seaman at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffness or formality of manner, from the substance used to stiffen linen collars.

clue.text: Chardonnay, perhaps foul? Bad, ten poured out inside

indicators.note: inside places the jumbled letters within the foul word

parts.note: vile means foul or disgusting

indicators.note: poured out suggests letters spilled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wine critic finds a white wine foul and bad, with ten glasses poured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like part of the surface judgment but is fodder with 'ten'; 'poured out' shuffles them, and 'inside' places that inside the word for foul. Vin de table is French for table wine.
explanation.definitionFit: French term for ordinary table wine, of which a cheap Chardonnay could be an example.

clue.text: Runs into large two-masted ship

indicators.note: into puts the runs letter inside the large word

parts.note: big means large
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A ship sails into a big two-masted vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A square-rigged sailing vessel carrying two masts is so named.

clue.text: Bone in shin, cushioned

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the run of letters

explanation.surface: A bone in the lower leg is well padded.
explanation.definitionFit: The small anvil-shaped bone in the middle ear is one of three ossicles.

clue.text: Jam found in pupil's first book!

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Someone spots jam on the opening page of a schoolchild's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit cooked with sugar is a conserve, a synonym for jam.

clue.text: Runner fell? Almost

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: a fell is an animal hide or skin

explanation.surface: A runner nearly fell over.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow runner fixed to a boot for gliding over snow.

clue.text: Outspoken, shocking court

parts.note: dire means dreadful or shocking

explanation.surface: Blunt words from an appalling law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and straightforward, saying things plainly without hedging.

clue.text: Prophet is excellent, a leader of Hebrews

parts.note: taken as written
A1, read as AI, means excellent

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A biblical seer is first-rate and a chief of the Hebrew people.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Testament prophet, author of the book bearing his name.

clue.text: Head after type showing benevolence

indicators.note: after puts the headland behind the type

parts.note: a kind is a type or sort
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A leader follows a certain sort, showing goodwill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being generous and considerate towards others, a synonym for goodwill.
